slot.brief: If α, β are roots of a quadratic, find a symmetric expression (e.g., α² + β² or α³ + β³) in terms of coefficients via Vieta.

stem: If $\alpha,\beta$ are the roots of $3x^2-5x+1=0$, find $\dfrac{\alpha^2}{\beta-1}+\dfrac{\beta^2}{\alpha-1}$.

verdicts.working: Using α+β=5/3 and αβ=1/3, the common denominator is (α−1)(β−1)=−1/3. The numerator is α³+β³−α²−β²=23/27, so the value is −23/9.

working:
$\alpha+\beta=\dfrac53,\quad \alpha\beta=\dfrac13$.
$\alpha^2+\beta^2=\left(\dfrac53\right)^2-2\left(\dfrac13\right)=\dfrac{19}{9}$.
$\alpha^3+\beta^3=\left(\dfrac53\right)^3-3\left(\dfrac13\right)\left(\dfrac53\right)=\dfrac{80}{27}$.
$\dfrac{\alpha^2}{\beta-1}+\dfrac{\beta^2}{\alpha-1}=\dfrac{\alpha^3+\beta^3-(\alpha^2+\beta^2)}{\alpha\beta-(\alpha+\beta)+1}=\dfrac{23/27}{-1/3}=-\dfrac{23}{9}$.

Independent check: Using α+β=5/3 and αβ=1/3, the common denominator is (α−1)(β−1)=−1/3. The numerator is α³+β³−α²−β²=23/27, so the value is −23/9.
solution:
Using $\alpha+\beta=\frac53$ and $\alpha\beta=\frac13$,
$$\alpha^2+\beta^2=\frac{19}{9},\qquad \alpha^3+\beta^3=\frac{80}{27}.$$
Thus the numerator over the common denominator is $\frac{80}{27}-\frac{19}{9}=\frac{23}{27}$, while $(\alpha-1)(\beta-1)=\frac13-\frac53+1=-\frac13$.
Hence the value is $\frac{23/27}{-1/3}=-\frac{23}{9}$.
